vignette: Saran, a 51-year-old South Eastern Asian man, has been married for over two decades. He works as a tax inspector and leads what appears to be an orderly life from the outside. However, Saran's world is shadowed by past trauma that continues to impact his daily existence. The abuse began subtly but escalated rapidly when he was 45 years old. His partner, whom he deeply loved and trusted, became increasingly controlling and aggressive over time. The turning point came during a particularly heated argument one evening; she lashed out physically, leaving Saran shaken and bruised both internally and externally. This incident marked the beginning of a cycle of abuse that would continue for several years. Saran's job as a tax inspector requires meticulous attention to detail and interaction with various individuals in often tense situations. Despite his professional competence, he has found it increasingly challenging to concentrate on his work since the abuse started. The trauma manifests in intrusive thoughts and vivid flashbacks during routine tasks. While reviewing financial documents at his desk, Saran's mind often drifts back to those moments of fear and helplessness. These intrusions are not only debilitating but also disrupt his professional performance. At home, Saran struggles with feelings of guilt and self-doubt. He questions whether he could have done something differently to prevent the abuse or if there is something inherently wrong with him that attracts such treatment. His relationship with his partner has become strained; while she no longer lives with him, her presence still looms large in his psyche. The fear of another confrontation lingers, causing him significant anxiety whenever he must interact with her, even during brief exchanges over their shared children. The couple's two teenage children observe this tension but do not fully understand the underlying cause, which adds to Saran's emotional burden. He worries about how his stress and trauma affect them, often finding himself more on edge when they are around. His once-robust bond with his family feels increasingly fragile due to the invisible weight of PTSD. Saran has developed a pattern of avoiding certain activities or places that remind him of the abuse. For instance, he no longer participates in community events where he might run into her friends or acquaintances. This avoidance extends to social interactions outside work; he finds himself withdrawing from gatherings and opting for solitary evenings instead, believing it's safer. Saran has also experienced significant sleep disturbances since the trauma began. Nightmares of the abuse episodes are frequent, leaving him exhausted and on edge during the day. Insomnia often compounds these issues, as he lies awake at night replaying conversations and scenarios that led to his current state. This lack of restful sleep exacerbates his irritability and impairs his cognitive function further. Despite the challenges, Saran remains dedicated to his role as a tax inspector because it provides him with a sense of normalcy and purpose. However, his heightened vigilance at work can sometimes lead to miscommunication or tension with colleagues. He is easily startled by sudden movements or loud noises in the office, which he tries to mask but finds increasingly difficult. Saran's daily routine now revolves around managing symptoms while trying to maintain a semblance of normalcy. His marriage remains intact, though it has evolved into a fragile alliance marked by careful negotiation and unspoken understandings. Saran is navigating this complex emotional terrain with the hope that time will ease his pain, but he finds himself questioning if healing can truly be achieved given the depth of his trauma. Each day brings its own set of challenges for Saran, as he grapples with the lingering effects of past abuse and strives to reclaim a sense of self-worth and safety in his life.
